summary: Defines a portion of the MIB for managed objects of a Fibre Channel Zone Server, which controls which devices can see each other. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Storage networks split devices into zones. This note defines the list of questions a management tool can ask about those zones.

questions: what is the fibre channel zone server mib
how to manage fibre channel zones with snmp
what is enhanced zoning in fibre channel
subtitle: SNMP objects for managing Fibre Channel zoning, the rules for which storage devices may talk to each other.

tldr.problem: Fibre Channel zoning limits which devices can communicate, but zones are normally set up through Fabric Zone Server requests, with no standard SNMP interface.
tldr.mechanism: Two MIB modules are defined. T11-FC-FABRIC-LOCK-MIB manages Fabric locks, and T11-FC-ZONE-SERVER-MIB models the Zone Set Database and the Active Zone Set for both Basic and Enhanced zoning.
tldr.outcome: Administrators can manage zoning over SNMP, but writable objects can change which hosts may connect, so SNMPv3 is RECOMMENDED. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

facts.label: Fabric Index on a single physical Fabric

today: RFC 4936 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2007. The unit data lists no obsoleting or updating RFC.

sections.title: What the MIB Is For
sections.content:
RFC 4936 describes managed objects for the Zone Server of a Fibre Channel network. It was previously approved by INCITS Task Group T11.5 and is a product of the IETF's IMSS working group.

It follows the Internet-Standard Management Framework: objects live in a MIB and are accessed mostly via SNMP, defined in SMIv2. It extends the Fibre Channel Management MIB (RFC 4044) to cover Zone Servers, both for Basic Zoning Management and for Enhanced Zoning Management as defined in FC-GS-5.
sections.eli5: Zones are the rules for who may play with whom. This document lets a manager read and change those rules from a distance.

sections.title: Zoning Concepts
sections.content:
Zones within a Fabric control frame delivery between Nx_Ports (hard zoning) or expose selected views of Name Server information (soft zoning). Communication is only possible when endpoints share a zone, similar to virtual private networks. Hard zoning is enforced in the switches; soft zoning relies on endpoints not sending traffic to an N_Port_ID they did not obtain from the Name Server.

Zone membership may be specified by the N_Port_Name, the N_Port_ID, the Node_Name, the F_Port_Name, or the Domain_ID and physical port number of the switch port. Zones are collected into a Zone Set, and a zone may be in more than one Zone Set. Only one Zone Set may be activated at a time.

The Active Zone Set is the one currently enforced, a Zone Set Database holds those available to activate, and a Zoning Database combines both.
sections.eli5: Devices are put into groups, and only members of the same group can talk. A zone set is a whole plan of groups that you switch on at once.

sections.title: Sessions, Locks and Commits
sections.content:
FC-GS-5 defines two request sets, Basic and Enhanced. Basic provides compatibility with FC-GS-4 and earlier. Enhanced may be used only if all switches in the Fabric support it.

In Enhanced zoning, writes to the Zoning Database happen inside a server session delimited by Server Session Begin (SSB) and Server Session End (SSE). On SSB the Zone Server locks the Fabric: the managing switch sends Acquire Change Authorization (ACA) to all other switches, and if any answers SW_RJT the SSB is rejected. SSE causes a Release Change Authorization (RCA).

Changes persist only if followed in the same session by a Commit Zone Changes (CMIT). The Zone Server checks consistency, sends a Stage Fabric Configuration Update (SFC) to the other switches, and if all accept, sends an Update Fabric Configuration (UFC) so the staged database becomes the Fabric's Zoning Database.
sections.eli5: To change the rules, one switch says "nobody else edit right now", makes the changes, checks them, and only then tells everyone to use the new rules.

sections.title: Two MIB Modules and Their Indexes
sections.content:
The document defines T11-FC-FABRIC-LOCK-MIB and T11-FC-ZONE-SERVER-MIB. The first supports FC-GS-5's generic capability of locking the Fabric for an application, such as Enhanced Zoning management, with one table in which each entry represents a switch acting as the managing switch of an application's Fabric lock.

Fabric-related tables are indexed by a Fabric Index (T11FabricIndex), which is 1 on a single physical Fabric. A switch is identified by fcmSwitchIndex within a management instance (fcmInstanceIndex), and that switch index is listed before the Fabric Index in an INDEX clause.

Locks made by ACA and by EACA both appear in t11FLockTable. A special Application_ID value assigned for this MIB marks ACA locks, so any active lock on a Fabric can be uniquely identified.
sections.eli5: One part of the MIB tracks who has the "do not disturb" sign up, and the other tracks the zones themselves.

sections.title: Basic and Enhanced Modes
sections.content:
The t11ZsServerOperationMode object tells whether a Fabric's Zone Server is in Basic or Enhanced mode. One set of objects covers what the modes share. Enhanced mode adds objects in t11ZsEnhancedModeGroup, which is only required for a server able to support Enhanced mode.

Basic-mode objects are expected to be implemented even in Enhanced mode, but their values are restricted or have no effect. For example, Basic mode distributes updates explicitly with t11ZsServerDistribute, whereas Enhanced mode distributes as part of commit using t11ZsServerCommit, so each has a fixed value in the other mode. Likewise t11ZsServerHardZoning only takes effect in Basic mode; in Enhanced mode t11ZsActiveZoneHardZoning sets hard zoning per zone.

One object, t11ZsServerDatabaseStorageType, sets the storage type for the whole Zone Server Database of a Fabric, to keep it consistent.
sections.eli5: There is an old way and a newer way to change zones. Some switches work in both, but the settings only count for the way currently in use.

sections.title: Zone Set Database and Active Zone Set
sections.content:
One Zone Set in the database can be activated to become the Active Zone Set. Changes to the database do not affect the Active Zone Set until a later activation. The Active Zone Set can also be reached directly with FC-GS-5 requests 'Activate Direct' and 'Get Active Zone Set'.

The Zone Server MIB models this with separate tables. Seven cover the database: t11ZsSetTable, t11ZsZoneTable, t11ZsSetZoneTable, t11ZsAliasTable, t11ZsZoneMemberTable, t11ZsAttribBlockTable and t11ZsAttribTable. Four cover the active set: t11ZsActiveTable, t11ZsActiveZoneTable, t11ZsActiveZoneMemberTable and t11ZsActiveAttribTable.
sections.eli5: There is a notebook of draft plans and one plan actually in force. Editing the notebook changes nothing until you pick a plan to switch on.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Unauthorized write access to any writable object could change the zoning information or activate an unauthorized Active Zone Set. That could allow unauthorized connectivity or deny authorized connectivity between hosts, suppress notifications, or cause unwanted ones.

Read access is sensitive too. The tables for the active zone set reveal currently authorized connectivity, while the database tables reveal potential alternative connectivity.

SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. Implementors are RECOMMENDED to use SNMPv3 with its cryptographic mechanisms, and deploying earlier versions is NOT RECOMMENDED. Operators must make sure only legitimate principals can GET or SET the objects.
sections.eli5: Whoever can edit the zone rules decides who can reach whose files, so only trusted people should hold the key, and the key should be a strong one.
